_comment: Golden regression fixture for the vertical slice.
Each case pins the OUTPUT OF THE PIPELINE POLICY -- which IPC sections get
auto-converted to BNS, which are held back for a human, and whether the case
routes to FIR, CSR, or officer review. It does NOT pin model accuracy;
If a change to ipc_bns_map.csv or cognizability.py alters any of these,
the test fails on purpose: these are legal decisions, not implementation
details, and every change to them should be deliberate and reviewed.

cases.name: dowry_death_all_high_confidence
cases.why: The DATASETS.md worked example. All four sections are high-confidence, so all four convert automatically and the cognizable offences force an FIR.
cases.narrative: The victim was harassed for dowry after marriage and later found dead at her matrimonial home.

cases.name: theft_single_section
cases.why: Simplest happy path: one high-confidence section, cognizable, straight to FIR. The value matters: the Schedule makes 303(2) non-cognizable under Rs 5,000.
cases.narrative: The accused stole a mobile phone worth Rs 15,000 from the complainant's shop.

cases.name: theft_without_value_is_conditional
cases.why: BNSS First Schedule splits 303(2) on property value (Rs 5,000). With no value in the complaint the entry is conditional and the officer must ask -- never a default FIR or CSR.
cases.narrative: The accused stole a mobile phone from the complainant's shop.

cases.name: theft_below_5000_is_non_cognizable
cases.why: Same section, value under the Schedule's threshold: non-cognizable, so CSR advisory.
cases.narrative: The accused stole a purse worth Rs 2,000 from the complainant.

cases.name: hurt_and_intimidation_all_non_cognizable
cases.why: Exercises the CSR branch: both sections map cleanly but neither is cognizable, so this is a Community Service Register entry, not an FIR.
cases.narrative: The neighbour slapped the complainant during an argument and threatened him.

cases.name: defamation_flagged_needs_review
cases.why: IPC 500 is confidence=med, needs_review=Y. It must NOT be auto-applied; with nothing left to act on the case goes to the officer.
cases.narrative: The accused published defamatory statements about the complainant.

cases.name: corruption_maps_to_other_statute
cases.why: IPC 161 is high-confidence but maps to the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, not the BNS. Auto-applying it would put a non-existent BNS section on an FIR, so it is always routed out.
cases.narrative: A public servant demanded a bribe to process the application.

cases.name: mischief_unprefixed_csv_value_is_repaired
cases.why: IPC 427 stores a bare '324(4),(5)' in the CSV. The loader must normalise it to a BNS-prefixed section rather than dropping the row. The Schedule classes 324(4) non-cognizable and 324(5) cognizable, so the composite cannot settle the route.
cases.narrative: The accused smashed the windows of the complainant's car.

cases.name: no_prediction_routes_to_officer
cases.why: An unrecognised complaint must never produce an empty FIR. Nothing predicted means the officer decides.
cases.narrative: The complainant reported a matter not covered by any rule.
